 🌍 Geographic Macro Overview
 🇺🇸 United States Mixed ↑ rates rising 
 Macro Stance: The Fed is in an active tightening posture — FOMC minutes released this week showed unanimous support for the September rate hike, with officials signaling another increase is likely this year.
Fiscal deficits remain structurally wide, and the 10Y yield has surged to 5.24% (↑5.4% vs 4 weeks ago), a level not seen in decades.

The 2Y sits at 4.06% (↑3.7%), and the curve has re-steepened to +119bps — this is no longer inversion stress but rather a term-premium repricing that reflects persistent supply-side pressure from Treasury issuance and sticky inflation expectations.
New / Most Important: The FOMC minutes confirmed hawkish unanimity — no dissent on the September hike, and language pointing to "another hike" this year.
Playbook ✓: Higher-for-longer rates benefiting large-cap quality over small-cap leverage plays — exactly as the textbook predicts when 10Y yields are above 5%.

Capital flow dynamics matter here: with the dollar presumably strong (high yields pulling global capital), the US is importing deflation for mega-cap multinationals while exporting rate stress to EM and small domestic firms.
Eurozone bond yields surged this week on energy price pressures, and the EU trade chief headed to China as trade tensions with Beijing came to a head.
Playbook ✓: Dollar strength vs euro on rate differentials — exactly as expected when US yields are climbing and European growth is weakening.
The yuan is under persistent depreciation pressure from the US-China rate differential — US 10Y at 5.24% creates enormous carry incentives for capital to exit China.

The fact that banks are raising fixed rates faster than the RBA signals that wholesale funding costs (driven by global yields, especially US 10Y at 5.24%) are now imposing tightening beyond what the RBA itself intends.
This is an imported tightening channel — US fiscal profligacy driving global yields higher is effectively setting Australian monetary conditions, regardless of what the RBA does.
| Playbook ✓: CEE FX weakness in a strong-dollar, high-US-yield environment is expected.

🌏 EM — Indonesia Bearish ↑ imported rate stress 
 Macro Stance: High US bond yields are directly shaking the Indonesian government bond market per Kompas.id — the classic EM vulnerability channel where rising US rates trigger local bond sell-offs, currency pressure, and forced tightening.
New / Most Important: Indonesia is the canary in the EM coal mine for US yield transmission.
With the US 10Y at 5.24% and climbing, EM local-currency bond markets face accelerating outflows.

This is the capital-flow mechanic that capitalflowresearch.com has long identified as the most powerful cross-border transmission channel: US fiscal dominance → higher Treasury yields → dollar strength → EM capital flight → EM central bank forced tightening → EM growth compression.
| ⚠️ Divergence: None — this is textbook, but the severity of US 10Y at 5.24% makes the transmission more acute than most models assumed.
⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention-break is that tech is rallying INTO a 5.24% 10Y yield.
Historically, long-duration growth stocks are the most rate-sensitive segment of the market.
The fact that Nasdaq is surging while yields climb suggests markets are pricing AI earnings growth as so dominant that discount rate effects are secondary.
